cues.en: I
cues.zh: I

cues.en: was born in Denbos where the painter, he, her name is Bos, named himself after.
cues.zh: 我出生在登博斯，那位画家，他，她名叫Bos，以自己的名字命名了那里。

cues.en: And so I've always been very fond of this painter who lived and worked in the fifteenth century.
cues.zh: 所以我一直非常喜欢这位生活在15世纪、在那里工作和创作的画家。

cues.en: And what is interesting about him in relation to morality is he lived at a time where religion's influence was waning, and he was sort of wondering, I think, what would happen with society if there was no religion or if there was less religion?
cues.zh: 他与道德的关联中有趣的一点是，他生活在一个宗教影响力日渐衰落的时代，我认为他在想，如果没有宗教或宗教减少，社会会变成什么样？

cues.en: And so he painted this famous painting, The Garden of Earthly Delights,
cues.zh: 于是他画了这幅著名的画作《人间乐园》，

cues.en: which some have interpreted as
cues.zh: 有些人将其解读为

cues.en: being humanity before the fall or being humanity without any fall at all. And so it makes you wonder what would happen if we hadn't tasted the fruit of knowledge, so to speak, and what kind of morality we would have.
cues.zh: 堕落之前的人类，或者根本没有堕落的人类。这让你不禁思考，如果我们没有尝过知识之果，可以说，我们会拥有什么样的道德。

cues.en: Much later, as a student, I went to a very different garden, a zoological garden in in Arnhem
cues.zh: 很久以后，作为一名学生，我去了一个截然不同的花园，阿纳姆的一个动物园

cues.en: where we keep chimpanzees. This is me at an early age with a baby chimpanzee.
cues.zh: 我们在那里饲养黑猩猩。这是我小时候和一只小黑猩猩的合影。

cues.en: And I discovered there that chimpanzees are very power hungry and wrote a book about it. And at that time, the focus in a lot of animal research was on aggression and competition. And I printed a whole picture of the animal kingdom and humanity included
cues.zh: 我在那里发现黑猩猩非常渴望权力，并写了一本关于此的书。当时，许多动物研究的焦点是攻击性和竞争。我描绘了一整幅动物王国包括人类的图景

cues.en: was that deep down we are competitors. We are aggressive.
cues.zh: 那就是在内心深处我们是竞争者。我们具有攻击性。

cues.en: We are all out for our own profit, basically.
cues.zh: 基本上，我们都追求自己的利益。

cues.en: This is the launch of my book. I'm not sure how well the chimpanzees read it, but they surely seemed interested in the book.
cues.zh: 这是我的新书发布会。我不确定黑猩猩们读得怎么样，但它们似乎对这本书很感兴趣。

cues.en: Now in the process of doing all this
cues.zh: 在做这些研究的过程中

cues.en: work on power and dominance and aggression and so on, I discovered that chimpanzees reconcile after fights.
cues.zh: 我研究权力、支配和攻击性等等，发现黑猩猩打斗后会和解。

cues.en: And so what you see here is two males who have had a fight. They ended up in a tree, and one of them holds out a hand to the other. And about a second after I took the picture, they came together in the fork of the tree, they kissed and embraced each other. Now this is very interesting because
cues.zh: 你们看这里，是两只打过架的雄性。它们最后到了树上，其中一只向另一只伸出手。我拍完照大约一秒后，它们在树杈处凑到一起，亲吻并拥抱了彼此。这非常有意思，因为

cues.en: at the time, everything was about competition and aggression, and so it wouldn't make any sense. The only thing that matters is that you win or that you lose. But why would you reconcile after a fight? That doesn't make any sense.
cues.zh: 当时一切研究都围绕竞争和攻击性，所以这说不通。唯一重要的是你赢或你输。但为什么打完架要和解呢？这完全说不通。

cues.en: This is the way bonobos do it. Bonobos do everything with sex, and so they also reconcile with sex. But the principle is exactly the same. The principle is that you have a valuable relationship
cues.zh: 倭黑猩猩是这么做的。倭黑猩猩什么事都用性来解决，所以它们也用性来和解。但原理完全一样。原理就是，你们有一段宝贵的关系

cues.en: that is damaged by conflict,
cues.zh: 被冲突破坏了，

cues.en: so you need to do something about it. And so my whole picture of the animal kingdom and including humans also started to change at that time.
cues.zh: 所以你得做点什么来修复。于是我对整个动物王国的图景，包括人类在内，也在那时开始改变。

cues.en: So we have this image in political science, economics, the humanities,
cues.zh: 在政治学、经济学、人文学科里，我们都有这样一种印象，

cues.en: philosophy for that matter,
cues.zh: 哲学里也是如此，

cues.en: that man is a wolf to man, and so deep down, our nature is actually nasty.
cues.zh: 就是人对人是狼，所以我们骨子里的本性其实是恶劣的。

cues.en: I think it's a very unfair image for the wolf.
cues.zh: 我觉得这对狼很不公平。

cues.en: The wolf is after all a very cooperative animal and that's why many of you have a dog at home which has all these characteristics also.
cues.zh: 狼毕竟是非常善于合作的动物，正因为如此，你们很多人家里养的狗也具备这些特征。

cues.en: And it's very unfair to humanity because humanity is actually much more cooperative and empathic than they're
cues.zh: 这对人类来说其实非常不公平，因为人类实际上比人们所认为的更加善于合作，也更富有同理心。

cues.en: given credit for. And so I started getting interested in those issues and studying that in other animals.
cues.zh: 所以我开始对这些问题产生兴趣，并开始研究其他动物身上的这些行为。

cues.en: So these are the pillars of morality.
cues.zh: 这些就是道德的基石。

cues.en: If you ask anyone what is morality based on, these are the two factors that always come out. One is reciprocity,
cues.zh: 如果你问任何人，道德建立在什么基础之上，答案总是离不开这两个因素。一个是互惠，

cues.en: and associated with it is a sense of justice and a sense of fairness,
cues.zh: 以及与之相关的正义感和公平感，

cues.en: and the other one is empathy and compassion. And human morality is more than this, but if you would remove these two pillars, there would be not much remaining, I think, and so they're absolutely essential. So let me give you a few examples here. This is a very old video from the Turkish primary center where they trained chimpanzees to cooperate.
cues.zh: 另一个是同理心和同情心。人类的道德内涵远不止这些，但我认为，如果去掉这两大基石，剩下的东西就所剩无几了。所以它们绝对不可或缺。接下来我给大家举几个例子。这是一段非常古老的视频，拍摄于土耳其的一个灵长类研究中心，当时他们在那里训练黑猩猩进行合作。

cues.en: So this is already about a hundred years ago that we were doing experiments
cues.zh: 早在大约一百年前，我们就已经开始做

cues.en: on cooperation.
cues.zh: 有关合作的实验了。

cues.en: And what you have here is two young chimpanzees
cues.zh: 你们现在看到的是两只年轻的黑猩猩，

cues.en: who have a box, and the box is too heavy for one chimp to pull in. And, of course, there's food on the box, otherwise, they wouldn't be pulling so hard.
cues.zh: 它们面前有一个箱子，但箱子太重了，单靠一只黑猩猩根本拉不动。当然，箱子上放着食物，否则它们也不会这么卖力地拉。

cues.en: And so they're bringing in the box,
cues.zh: 于是，它们开始一起把箱子拉过来，

cues.en: and you can see that they're synchronized.
cues.zh: 你们可以看到，它们的动作非常同步。

cues.en: You can see that they work together. They pull at the same moment. It's already a big advance over over many other animals who wouldn't be able to do that. And now you're gonna get a more interesting picture because now one of the two chimps
cues.zh: 可以看到，它们正在协同合作，在同一时刻一起发力。这已经比许多其他动物强出一大截，因为那些动物根本做不到这一点。接下来，你们会看到更有意思的情况，因为现在这两只黑猩猩中，有一只

cues.en: has been fed. So one of the two is not really interested in the task anymore.
cues.zh: 已经吃过东西了。所以其中一只对这项任务已经不怎么感兴趣了。

cues.en: Now look at what happens at the very end of this.
cues.zh: 现在看看最后发生了什么。

cues.en: He he takes basically everything.
cues.zh: 他几乎拿走了所有东西。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: so there are two interesting parts about this. One is that the chimp on the right has a full understanding he needs to partner, so full understanding of the need for cooperation.
cues.zh: 所以这里有两个有趣的点。一是右边的黑猩猩完全理解它需要伙伴，也就是完全理解合作的必要性。

cues.en: The second one is that the partner is willing to work even though he's not interested in the food. Why would that be? Well, that probably has to do with reciprocity. There's actually a lot of evidence in in primates and other animals that they return favors, so he will get a return favor at some point in the future. And so that's how this all operates.
cues.zh: 第二点是，伙伴愿意合作，尽管它对食物并不感兴趣。为什么会这样？这大概和互惠有关。实际上，有大量证据表明灵长类和其他动物会回报恩惠，所以它在未来某个时候会得到回报。这就是这一切运作的方式。

cues.en: We do the same task with elephants. Now with elephants, it's very dangerous to work with elephants. And another problem with elephants is that you cannot make an apparatus that is too heavy for a single elephant.
cues.zh: 我们用大象做同样的任务。和大象合作非常危险。大象的另一个问题是，你没法做一个对单只大象来说太重而拉不动的装置。

cues.en: Now you can probably make it, but it's going to be pretty clumsy apparatus, I think. And so what we did in their case, we do these studies in Thailand with Josh Plotnick, is we have an apparatus around of which there's a rope, a single rope. And if you pull on this side of the rope, the rope disappears on the other side. So two elephants need to pick it up at exactly the same time and pull. Otherwise, nothing is going to happen and the rope disappears.
cues.zh: 你现在大概能做出来，但我觉得那会是个相当笨拙的装置。所以在大象的案例中，我们在泰国和 Josh Plotnick 做了这些研究，我们设置了一个装置，上面有一根绳子，一根单绳。如果你拉绳子的这一边，绳子就会从另一边消失。所以两只大象需要完全同时抓起它并拉动。否则什么都不会发生，绳子会消失。

cues.en: And so the first tape you're going to see is two elephants who are released together, arrive at the apparatus. The apparatus is on the left with food on it. And so they come together, they arrive together, they pick it up together and they pull together. So it's it's actually fairly simple for them.
cues.zh: 所以你们将要看到的第一段录像，是两只大象被同时放出来，到达装置前。装置在左边，上面放着食物。所以它们一起过来，一起到达，一起抓起绳子，一起拉。所以这对它们来说其实相当简单。

cues.en: There they are.
cues.zh: 它们在那儿。

cues.en: And so that's how they bring it in. But now we're gonna make it more difficult because the the whole purpose of this experiment is to see how well they understand cooperation. Do they understand it as well as the chimps, for example? And so what we do in the next step is we release one elephant before the other, and that elephant needs to be smart enough to stay there and wait and not pull at the rope because if he pulls at the rope, it disappears and the whole test is over. Now this elephant does something illegal
cues.zh: 它们就是这样把绳子拉过来的。但现在我们要增加难度，因为这个实验的整个目的就是看它们对合作的理解有多深。比如，它们能像黑猩猩那样理解吗？所以下一步我们要做的是，先放出一头大象，再放另一头，而先放出的那头得足够聪明，待在那儿等着，不去拉绳子，因为一拉绳子，绳子就消失了，整个测试也就结束了。而这头大象做了一件违规的事

cues.en: that we did not teach it,
cues.zh: 我们并没教过它，

cues.en: but it shows the understanding that he has because he puts his big foot on the rope, stands on the rope and waits there for the other and then the other is gonna do all the work for him. So so it's it's what we call freeloading.
cues.zh: 但这说明它有那样的理解力，因为它把大脚踩在绳子上，站在绳子上等着另一头，然后让另一头替它干所有的活儿。这就是我们所说的搭便车。

cues.en: But but it shows the intelligence that the elephants had. They they developed several of these alternative techniques that we did not approve of necessarily.
cues.zh: 但这展现了这些大象的智慧。它们琢磨出了好几种我们未必认可的替代技巧。

cues.en: So the other elephant is now coming
cues.zh: 现在另一头大象过来了

cues.en: and is going to pull it in.
cues.zh: 准备把绳子拉过来。

cues.en: Now look at the other. The other doesn't forget to eat, of course.
cues.zh: 现在看另一头。另一头当然不会忘了吃。

cues.en: This was the cooperation reciprocity part. Now something on empathy. Empathy is my main topic at the moment of research, and empathy has sort of two qualities. One is understanding part of it. This is just a regular definition, the ability to understand
cues.zh: 这就是合作互惠的部分。现在说说共情。共情是我目前研究的主要课题，共情大致有两个特质。一个是理解的部分。这只是个常规定义，即理解

cues.en: and share the feelings of another, and the emotional part. And so empathy has basically two channels.
cues.zh: 并分享他人感受的能力，还有情感的部分。所以共情基本上有两个通道。

cues.en: One is the body channel. If you talk with a sad person, you're going to adopt a sad expression
cues.zh: 一种是身体通道。如果你和一个悲伤的人交谈，你也会不自觉地露出悲伤的表情

cues.en: and a sad posture and before you know it, you feel sad. And that's sort of the the body channel of emotional
cues.zh: 摆出悲伤的姿势，不知不觉间，你自己也会感到悲伤。这就是情绪共情的身体通道

cues.en: empathy
cues.zh: 情绪共情

cues.en: which many animals have. Your average dog has that also. That's actually why people keep mammals in the home and not turtles or snakes or something like that who don't have that kind of empathy. And then there's a cognitive channel which is more that you can take the perspective of somebody else, and and that's more limited. There's few animals. I think elephants and apes can do that kind of thing, but there are very few animals who can do that.
cues.zh: 很多动物都有这种能力。普通的狗也有这种能力。事实上，这就是人们为什么喜欢在家里养哺乳动物，而不是乌龟、蛇之类的动物，因为后者不具备这种共情能力。除此之外，还有一种认知通道，也就是你能够站在别人的角度思考问题。这种能力就比较有限了。只有少数动物具备这种能力。我认为大象和猿类能够做到这一点，但真正具备这种能力的动物非常少。

cues.en: So synchronization,
cues.zh: 所以，同步行为，

cues.en: which is part of that whole empathy mechanism, is a very old one in the animal kingdom.
cues.zh: 作为整个共情机制的一部分，在动物界已经存在了非常久。

cues.en: And in humans, of course, we can study that with yawn contagion.
cues.zh: 当然，在人类身上，我们可以通过哈欠传染现象来研究这种行为。

cues.en: Humans yawn when others yawn, and it's related to empathy. It activates
cues.zh: 看到别人打哈欠时，人也会跟着打哈欠，而且这与共情有关。它会激活

cues.en: the same areas in the brain. Also, know that people who have a lot of yawn contagion are highly empathic.
cues.zh: 大脑中相同的区域。另外要知道，容易被哈欠传染的人，通常具有很强的共情能力。

cues.en: People who have problems with empathy such as autistic children, they don't have yawn contagion. So it is connected. And we study that in our chimpanzees by presenting them with an animated head. So that's what you see on the upper left, an animated head that yawns, and there's a chimpanzee watching, an actual real chimpanzee watching a computer screen on which we play these animations.
cues.zh: 存在共情障碍的人，比如自闭症儿童，就不会出现哈欠传染现象。所以两者确实有关联。我们通过向黑猩猩展示一个动画头像来研究这一现象。你们在左上方看到的就是这个动画头像，它正在打哈欠，而一只黑猩猩正在观看。这里是真正的黑猩猩，它正盯着电脑屏幕，我们在屏幕上播放这些动画。

cues.en: And so yawn contagion that you're probably all familiar with
cues.zh: 所以打哈欠会传染，你们大概都很熟悉

cues.en: and maybe you're going to start yawning soon now
cues.zh: 也许你们很快也要开始打哈欠了

cues.en: is something that we share with other animals. That's related to that whole body channel of synchronization that underlies empathy
cues.zh: 这是我们和其他动物共有的现象。这和同理心背后的全身同步通道有关

cues.en: and that is universal in the mammals basically.
cues.zh: 基本上在哺乳动物中这是普遍存在的。

cues.en: Now we also study more complex expressions. This is consolation. This is a male chimpanzee who has lost a fight and he's screaming and a juvenile comes over and puts an arm around him and calms him down. That's consolation. It's very similar to human consolation.
cues.zh: 我们还研究了更复杂的表达。这是安慰行为。这是一只雄性黑猩猩，它打输了架正在尖叫，一只幼崽走过来搂住它，让它平静下来。这就是安慰。和人类的安慰非常相似。

cues.en: And consolation behavior
cues.zh: 而安慰行为

cues.en: It's empathy driven.
cues.zh: 是由同理心驱动的。

cues.en: That's actually the way they study empathy in human children is to instruct a family member to act distressed and then they see what young children do. And so it is related to empathy and that's the kind of expressions we look at. We also recently published an experiment, you may have heard about it, on altruism in chimpanzees
cues.zh: 实际上，研究人类儿童同理心的方法就是这样：让家庭成员假装难过，然后观察年幼的孩子怎么做。所以这和同理心有关，这就是我们观察的那类表达。我们最近还发表了一个实验，你们可能听说过，是关于黑猩猩的利他行为

cues.en: where the question is, do chimpanzees care about the welfare of somebody else? And for decades,
cues.zh: 问题是，黑猩猩会关心别人的福祉吗？几十年来，

cues.en: it had been assumed that only humans can do that, that only humans worry about the welfare of somebody else. Now we did a very simple experiment.
cues.zh: 人们一直认为只有人类才能做到这一点，只有人类才会关心别人的福祉。我们做了一个非常简单的实验。

cues.en: We do that on chimpanzees that live in Lawrenceville
cues.zh: 我们在住在Lawrenceville的黑猩猩身上做这个实验

cues.en: in in the field station of Yerkes, and so that... That's how they live, and we call them into a room and do experiments with them. In this case, we put two chimpanzees side by side and one has a bucket full of tokens and the tokens have different meanings. One kind of token feeds only the partner who chooses, the other one feeds both of them. So this this is a study we did with Vicky Horner.
cues.zh: 在Yerkes的野外研究站，它们就是这样生活的，我们把它们叫进一个房间做实验。在这个实验中，我们把两只黑猩猩并排放置，一只有一个装满代币的桶，代币有不同的含义。一种代币只喂做出选择的那只，另一种则喂它们两个。这是我和Vicky Horner一起做的一项研究。

cues.en: And here you have the two color tokens.
cues.zh: 这里有两枚彩色代币。

cues.en: So they have a whole bucket full of them
cues.zh: 它们有一整桶这种代币

cues.en: and they have to pick one of the two colors.
cues.zh: 而且必须从两种颜色里选一个。

cues.en: You will see how that goes.
cues.zh: 看看会怎么样。

cues.en: So if this chimp makes the selfish choice,
cues.zh: 所以如果这只黑猩猩做出自私的选择，

cues.en: which is the red token in this case,
cues.zh: 在这个情况下就是红色代币，

cues.en: needs to give it to us, we pick it up, we put it on the table where there's two food rewards, but in this case only the one on the right gets food and the one on the left walks away because she knows already that this is not a good test for her. Then the next one is the pro social token.
cues.zh: 她需要把它交给我们，我们接过来放到桌上，那里有两份食物奖励，但这次只有右边那只得到食物，左边那只走开了，因为她已经知道这对自己不是个好测试。接下来是亲社会代币。

cues.en: So the one who makes the choices, that's the interesting part here. For the one who makes the choices,
cues.zh: 所以做选择的那只，这才是这里有趣的地方。对做选择的那只来说，

cues.en: it doesn't really matter. So she gives us now a pro social token and both chimps get fed. So the one who makes the choices always get a reward. So it doesn't matter whatsoever and she should actually be choosing blindly.
cues.zh: 其实无所谓。现在她交给我们一个亲社会代币，两只黑猩猩都能吃到食物。所以做选择的那只总能得到奖励。因此这完全无所谓，她其实应该是在盲选。

cues.en: But what we find is that they prefer the prosocial token. So this is the 50% line. That's the random expectation and especially if the partner draws attention to itself, they they choose more. And if the partner puts pressure on them, so if the partner starts spitting water and intimidating them, then the choices go down and they actually don't want to... It's as if they're saying, if you're not behaving, I'm not going to be pro social today. And this is what happens without a partner, when there's no partner sitting there. And so we found that the chimpanzees do care about the well-being of somebody else, especially these are other members of their own group.
cues.zh: 但我们发现，它们更偏好亲社会代币。所以这是50%线。那是随机预期，尤其是当同伴引起它注意时，它们会选得更多。而如果同伴给它们施压，比如同伴开始喷水、恐吓它们，选择就会减少，它们其实不想……就像在说：如果你不守规矩，我今天就不亲社会了。而没有同伴时，也就是没有同伴坐在那里时，情况就是这样。所以我们发现，黑猩猩确实会关心别人的福祉，尤其是这些还是它们自己群体的成员。

cues.en: So a final experiment that I want to mention to you is our fairness study.
cues.zh: 最后我想提一个实验，就是我们的公平性研究。

cues.en: And so this
cues.zh: 于是这个

cues.en: became a very famous study and there's now many more because after we did this about ten years ago,
cues.zh: 研究变得非常有名，现在还有很多类似研究，因为大约十年前我们做了这个实验之后，

cues.en: it became very well known. And we did that originally with capuchin monkeys, and I'm going to show you the first experiment that we did. It has now been done with dogs and with birds
cues.zh: 它就广为人知了。我们最初是用卷尾猴做的，我要给你们看我们做的第一个实验。现在这个实验已经在狗和鸟身上做过了，

cues.en: and with chimpanzees,
cues.zh: 还有黑猩猩，

cues.en: with with sire blossom, we started out with capuchin monkeys.
cues.zh: 跟跟sire blossom，我们一开始用的是卷尾猴。

cues.en: So what we did is we put two capuchin monkeys side by side. Again, these animals, they live in a group. They know each other. We take them out of the group, put them in a test chamber.
cues.zh: 我们的做法是把两只卷尾猴并排放在一起。再说一次，这些动物是群居的，它们彼此认识。我们把它们从群体中带出来，放进测试室。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 然后

cues.en: there's a very simple task that they need to do. And if you give both of them cucumber
cues.zh: 它们需要完成一个非常简单的任务。如果你给它们俩都发黄瓜

cues.en: for the task, the two monkeys side by side, they're perfectly willing to do this 25 times in a row. So cucumber, even though it's really only water in my opinion, but cucumber
cues.zh: 作为完成任务的奖励，两只猴子并排待着，它们完全愿意连续做25次。所以黄瓜，虽然在我看来其实只是水，但黄瓜

cues.en: is perfectly fine for them. Now if you give the partner grapes,
cues.zh: 对它们来说完全没问题。现在如果你给同伴葡萄，

cues.en: the food preferences of my capuchin monkeys correspond exactly with the prices in the supermarket.
cues.zh: 我的卷尾猴的食物偏好和超市里的价格完全对应。

cues.en: And so if you give them grapes as a far better food,
cues.zh: 所以如果你给它们葡萄这种好得多的食物，

cues.en: then you create inequity between them.
cues.zh: 那就在它们之间制造了不公平。

cues.en: So that's the experiment we did. Recently, we videotaped it with new monkeys who had never done the task thinking that maybe they would have a stronger reaction, that turned out to be right. The one on the left is a monkey who gets cucumber. The one on the right is the one who gets grapes.
cues.zh: 这就是我们做的实验。最近，我们用从未做过这个任务的新猴子录了像，想着也许它们会有更强烈的反应，结果证明是对的。左边那只猴子拿到的是黄瓜。右边那只拿到的是葡萄。

cues.en: The one who gets cucumber, note that the first piece of cucumber is perfectly fine. The first piece she eats,
cues.zh: 拿到黄瓜的那只，注意第一块黄瓜完全没问题。她吃下第一块，

cues.en: then she sees the other one getting grape, and you will see what happens.
cues.zh: 然后她看到另一只拿到了葡萄，接下来你会看到发生了什么。

cues.en: So she gives a rock to us. That's the task.
cues.zh: 于是她递给我们一块石头。这就是任务。

cues.en: And we give her a piece of cucumber and she eats it. The other one needs to give a rock to us.
cues.zh: 我们给她一块黄瓜，她吃了。另一只需要递给我们一块石头。

cues.en: And that's what she does.
cues.zh: 她照做了。

cues.en: And she gets a grape
cues.zh: 然后她得到了一颗葡萄，

cues.en: each of the other one sees that,
cues.zh: 另一只看到这个情况，

cues.en: she gives a rock to us now, gets again cucumber.
cues.zh: 现在她递给我们一块石头，又拿到了黄瓜。

cues.en: She tests a rock now
cues.zh: 她现在拿石头试了试，

cues.en: against the wall. She needs to give it to us
cues.zh: 对着墙。她需要把它递给我们，

cues.en: and she gets cucumber again.
cues.zh: 然后又得到了黄瓜。

cues.en: So this is basically the Wall Street protest that you see here.
cues.zh: 所以这基本上就是你们在这里看到的华尔街抗议。

cues.en: Let let me tell you... I I still have two minutes left. Let me tell you a funny story about this. This this study became very famous and we got a lot of comments, especially anthropologists,
cues.zh: 让我告诉你们……我还剩两分钟。让我讲一个关于这个的有趣故事。这项研究变得非常有名，我们收到了很多评论，尤其是来自人类学家、

cues.en: economists,
cues.zh: 经济学家、

cues.en: philosophers. They didn't like this at all because they had decided in their mind, I believe, that fairness
cues.zh: 哲学家的。他们完全不喜欢这个，因为我相信他们心里已经认定，公平

cues.en: is a very complex issue and that animals cannot have it. And so one philosopher even wrote us that it was impossible that monkeys had a sense of fairness because fairness was invented during the French Revolution.
cues.zh: 是一个非常复杂的问题，动物不可能拥有它。于是一位哲学家甚至写信给我们说，猴子不可能有公平感，因为公平是法国大革命期间发明的。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: now...
cues.zh: 现在……

cues.en: And another one wrote a whole chapter saying that he would believe it had something to do with fairness if the one who got grapes would refuse the grapes. Now the funny thing is that Sarah Brosnan, who's been doing this with chimpanzees, had a couple of combinations of chimpanzees where indeed
cues.zh: 另一位写了一整章，说如果拿到葡萄的那只会拒绝葡萄，他才相信这与公平有关。有趣的是，一直用黑猩猩做这个实验的 Sarah Brosnan 遇到过几组黑猩猩组合，其中确实

cues.en: the one who would get the grape would refuse the grape until the other guy also got a grape. So we're getting very close to the human sense of fairness, and I think philosophers need to rethink their philosophy for a while.
cues.zh: 拿到葡萄的那只会拒绝葡萄，直到另一只也拿到葡萄。所以我们非常接近人类的公平感，我认为哲学家们需要重新思考一下他们的哲学了。

cues.en: So let me summarize.
cues.zh: 那我总结一下。

cues.en: I believe there's an evolved morality. I think morality is much more than what I've been talking about, but it would be impossible without these ingredients that we find in other primates, which are empathy and consolation,
cues.zh: 我相信存在一种进化而来的道德。我认为道德远不止我刚讲的内容，但如果没有我们在其他灵长类动物身上发现的这些要素——共情和安慰，

cues.en: prosocial tendencies,
cues.zh: 亲社会倾向，

cues.en: and reciprocity and a sense of fairness. And so we work on these particular issues to see if we can create a morality from the bottom up, so to speak, without necessarily God and religion involved and to see how we can get to an evolved morality.
cues.zh: 互惠和公平感——道德就不可能存在。所以我们研究这些具体问题，看看能否可以说自下而上地构建一种道德，不一定涉及上帝和宗教，看看我们如何走向一种进化而来的道德。

cues.en: And I thank you for your attention.
cues.zh: 谢谢大家的关注。
